# KRAKEN and KRAKENC reference artifacts

Generated by Acoustics Toolbox v2023.5, commit
`475108519289c6fb488b58980c644ea14eccc604`, not by Rust. The pinned
`tools/reference/Dockerfile` uses Linux x86-64, GNU Fortran 12.2.0
(Debian 12.2.0-14+deb12u1), and
`-O1 -ffast-math -funroll-all-loops -fomit-frame-pointer -std=gnu`.

`PekerisBroadband.env` derives from Pekeris by changing the title, adding
`B` in the sixth top-option slot, selecting `W` loss and 0.8 dB/wavelength
bottom attenuation, NG 1000→101, RMax 2→1000 km, and appending three
frequencies in the order 75/50/62.5 Hz. Its `.flp` changes only the title.
`PekerisComplexBroadband` changes only the title and cHigh 1700→2000 m/s.
Both use mesh multipliers 1/2/4: at 75 Hz the intervals are 151/303/606,
at 50 Hz 101/202/404, and at 62.5 Hz 126/252/505. Three pinned runs per
pair yield identical `.mod/.shd` binaries. Committed and fresh comparisons
check all frequencies, with 5/3/4 KRAKEN or 7/4/6 KRAKENC modes and nine
line-source pressures per frequency. **They are derived inputs, not the
original BroadBand/MunkK.**

The **unmodified upstream** `tests/BroadBand/MunkK.env/.flp` is separately
compared through **KRAKEN** in fresh pinned CI at 50/500 Hz: 102/1,023 modes and 501,501 pressures
per frequency (1,003,002 total). Input SHA-256 is respectively
`9ccab68c7ace7525904e6761d52056dc141fb4e1ca6c43929c86e9a22b5986c9` /
`97e8d768e3b7e48948539913f56b2dd5dfc71406bfeef49271bf63209912588f`.
Three runs yielded identical `.mod/.shd` SHA-256
`58d9ea25379bce98f17c5b59c7ffd3e9680984fadc8ee8bc59daeaacbdcfb4e3` /
`6cd0811cc1985fb70a78e3ac510dfd7b501a7cff21208cd7ea66be339d65ba20`.
Original binaries stay out of Git. This pair differs from the original
single-frequency `tests/Munk/MunkK`, which remains a separate regression.

`PekerisComplex.env` derives from Pekeris by enabling KRAKENC restarts
(`NVN .`), raising cHigh from 1700 to 2000 m/s, and setting RMax to 0.
`PekerisComplexBlank` changes only the restart option to the valid default
`NVN`; the pinned Fortran modal table and binary equal PekerisComplex, so its
offline test reuses those goldens, while fresh CI runs both inputs separately.
`PekerisComplexSlow` changes only the bottom speed from 1700 to 1400 m/s;
its four modes all radiate into the bottom and have their own `.mod/.prt`.
`PekerisComplexCLow` changes the blank-restart case's cLow from 1400 to
1550 m/s: its first mode is out of band, while the remaining three have their
own `.mod/.prt`. The blank setting produces a stable three-mode v2023.5
reference; Fortran's dotted random-restart option sometimes also emits the
out-of-band mode for this input, so that variant is not a reproducible oracle.
`PekerisComplexRefined.env` derives from PekerisComplexBlank by changing the
title, NG 1000→100 and RMax 0→1000 km; its `.flp` changes only the title. The
pinned solver uses mesh multipliers 1/2/4. Three runs produced identical
`.mod/.shd` binaries; all four modes and nine pressures match the committed
goldens and fresh CI.
`PekerisComplexBlank.flp` is a **separately derived** coherent line-source FIELD
input with nine pressures. Its committed `.shd` binary matches a second pinned
Fortran run; its `.mod` binary is unchanged and reuses the PekerisComplex
modes golden.
`PekerisComplexGradient` changes only the 100 m water SSP point from 1500 to
1520 m/s relative to PekerisComplexBlank; `PekerisComplexReverseGradient`
reverses that 1500→1520 m/s gradient. Pinned Fortran blank-restart runs
returned identical `.mod` binaries three times per case; their own `.mod/.prt`
check all four modes including one leaky mode each. Both are **derived**, not
original MunkKleaky or sduct inputs.
`MunkLeakyPartial.env` starts from upstream `tests/MunkLeaky/MunkKleaky.env`
(SHA-256 `176a4e2f9c3b142d9f58c2fc691374a789b470322bfd44eb5679da754604e60a`).
It retains exactly the first seven water SSP records (0–1000 m) and the 50 Hz
frequency, bottom speed/density and `RMax=0`; changes the title, depth
5000→1000 m, NG 5000→800, `NVW .`→`NVN` (blank restarts), bottom attenuation
0.8→0 dB/wavelength, cHigh 20000→1700 m/s, and source/receiver mode-sampling
depths. `MunkLeakyPartialLoss` changes only the derived bottom attenuation
from 0 to the original 0.8 dB/wavelength `W` loss. Three pinned Fortran runs
per derived case yielded identical `.mod` binaries: 30 modes, nine leaky each.
A **separately derived** coherent point-source `MunkLeakyPartialLoss.flp`
selects two source depths, six receiver depths, three ranges (including zero)
and nonnegative offsets; the original `.env`-derived modal sampling grid is
unchanged. Three pinned Fortran runs yielded identical `.mod` and `.shd`
binaries; 36 complex pressures match a committed `.shd` golden and fresh CI.
`MunkLeakyPartialC.env` changes only `N`→`C` relative to the lossy derivative;
its separately derived `.flp` changes only the title. Three pinned runs
produced identical `.mod/.shd` binaries (30 modes, nine leaky; 36 pressures)
and all samples match committed goldens and fresh CI. **These are derived
inputs, not original MunkKwb/Kbb or sductK examples.**
The **unmodified upstream** `MunkKleaky.env` (same SHA above) and `.flp`
(SHA-256 `72b6e29b05b048bf8fc5dc67559ba1c037ff8f82455e93d83ce81777f207e4e6`)
are separately compared with fresh pinned Fortran in CI: 329 complex modes,
every mode sample, attenuation, group speed and all 150,801 complex pressures.
Three local pinned Fortran runs of the original pair produced identical `.mod`
and `.shd` binaries. The `.env` determines modal samples; the original `.flp`
provides FIELD geometry. Four other **unmodified** pairs are compared in
fresh pinned CI: `MunkKwb.env/.flp` (63 modes, 150,801 pressures),
`MunkKbb.env/.flp` (102, 150,801), `sductK.env/.flp` (1,077, 201,201) and
`calibK.env/.flp` (33, 101,101; mesh multipliers 1/2/4).
Their SHA-256 input pairs are respectively
`5f422c8b0b5ced56c88d280e740057adc94e00f4d88c25292a17c51f8d3888b7` /
`72b6e29b05b048bf8fc5dc67559ba1c037ff8f82455e93d83ce81777f207e4e6`,

The final pair is upstream `tests/calib/calibK`; the preceding three use the
paths documented in the compatibility matrix. Three pinned runs of each original pair yielded identical `.mod/.shd`
binaries. No original `.mod/.shd` binary is committed.
A 10,000× depth / 10,000× inverse-frequency scaling of `PekerisComplex` is
tested metamorphically against the original modes to guard root separation;
it is **not** claimed as a fresh Fortran acceptance (the pinned solver returns
only three modes with blank restarts and has variable small imaginary roundoff
with dotted restarts at that scale).
The remaining **derived inputs** have no `.flp` or FIELD goldens: modes-only
tests use `Pekeris.flp` solely for valid geometry; the `.env` determines modal
sampling depths. The pinned `krakenc-fortran` reference produces `.mod/.prt`
and FIELD produces `.shd` for four single-frequency derived fixtures, the
broadband Pekeris derivative and five original pairs; committed binaries are
unmodified and `.prt` files have trailing spaces removed. The same comparator
checks all ten single-frequency derived cases, the broadband derivative and
five original pairs in fresh CI, including every complex32 wavenumber, phase-aligned shape,
print precision and attenuation. It also checks every complex pressure for
all five derived FIELD fixtures and five original pairs. These acceptances do not
imply general KRAKENC FIELD support outside the coherent single-profile subset.
`PekerisRigid`/`PekerisRigidLoss` change only the surface from `V` to `R`
(relative to Pekeris/PekerisDenseLoss respectively) and use distinct titles.
They are **derived fixtures**, not unmodified upstream examples.
`PekerisHard` and `PekerisHardBoth` derive from PekerisSpline3, replace the
acoustic bottom record with a rigid condition (and `cHigh=2000` m/s), and
exercise vacuum/rigid surfaces respectively. They are **not** official inputs.
`PekerisRigidPlane` is another **derived input**, constructed for the exact
rigid-rigid plane-mode endpoint; it is not an upstream example. Its 17-point
base mesh and refined meshes keep the same two Fortran modes.
`MunkLossless` replaces `NVW` with `NVN`, bottom loss `0.8` with `0`,
and limits receiver/mode/field grids. `MunkBottomLoss` retains the upstream
loss and profile but also reduces the grids (not an original upstream input).
`MunkAnalytic.env` changes the original `tests/Munk/MunkAnalytic.env` title,
mesh count (0 → 2000), and RMax (200 → 0 km); its `.flp` is a new coherent
line-source FIELD input. The original `.env` SHA-256 is
`3cc2a2121d9ae3ff395fc138ef31656f907f09d57a195fd9bdda77f42bf37162`.
It is **derived**, not a comparison of the unmodified official pair. The
original auto-mesh/extrapolated **`.env`** is separately compared in CI
against fresh Fortran `.mod/.prt` with a derived coherent FIELD `.flp`, under
the same exact complex32 `.mod` check. The original three-line `.flp` cannot
be parsed by the pinned v2023.5 FIELD; it is not an accepted original pair.
The sduct-derived inputs restrict cHigh from 100000 m/s to the 1523.9 m/s
bottom speed and limit the coordinate grids. `SductTrapped` replaces `CVW`
with `CVN`; `SductPchip` uses `PVW` and explicitly specifies 0.8 dB/wavelength
bottom loss; `SductSpline` uses lossless `SVN`. These are **not** comparisons
to the unmodified official examples. **CI separately compares the unmodified upstream MunkK
`.env/.flp` end to end** (102 modes, 501,501 pressure samples) against the pinned
Fortran output, plus the unmodified MunkAnalytic `.env` with separately derived
coherent FIELD input (102 modes, 25 pressure samples). Unmodified sductK is separately compared end-to-end via KRAKENC, not KRAKEN.
`tests/PekerisRD` upstream is a BELLHOP case, not a KRAKEN oracle.

Re-run fresh numerical comparisons from the repository root:

```sh
for case in Pekeris PekerisFiltered PekerisDense PekerisDenseLoss PekerisRefined PekerisSpline3 PekerisRigid PekerisRigidLoss PekerisHard PekerisHardBoth PekerisRigidPlane MunkLossless MunkBottomLoss MunkAnalytic SductTrapped SductPchip SductSpline; do
  tools/reference/compare-kraken.sh "crates/kraken/tests/fixtures/$case.env"
done
```

Fresh files go to `target/reference/$case-kraken/`. To update a golden, review
numerical changes first, copy its `.mod/.shd/.prt` here, trim trailing whitespace
from `.prt` lines, and update hashes below. Binary files are unmodified; `.prt`
CPU timings are nondeterministic, so the test reads only its modal table.
The test-only reader is `../../differential_reference.rs`. For broadband
regeneration commands, see [tools/README.md](../../../../../tools/README.md).
It compares all per-frequency record blocks and includes a later-frequency
corruption check; it never treats the first block as the entire file.

One comparator runs on committed files without Docker and fresh Fortran files
in CI. It checks counts, coordinates, frequency, printed and binary wavenumbers,
attenuation, phase/group speeds, unit-phase-aligned shapes **without amplitude
rescaling**, and every complex pressure. Tolerances: printed k `5e-10`,
shapes `1e-6`, pressure `2e-6`, group speed `0.005` (two decimal print digits).
Lossless binary complex32 wavenumbers must match exactly; with bottom loss,
the imaginary binary component has a `1e-10` absolute bound (measured max
`5.83e-11` on the independent 3 dB/wavelength fixture); the real component
still matches exactly. The imaginary part depends on first-mesh roots and
Fortran's complex-square-root rounding. Printed loss uses its `G10.2` half-last-digit precision.
The public attenuation is positive `-Im(k)`, whereas `.prt` prints signed `Im(k)`.

## KRAKENC cubic/analytic profile provenance

This slice reuses the existing **real/lossless** PCHIP/spline/analytic `Profile`,
not a complex-valued or lossy-water interpolation implementation. A-bottom
W attenuation and the existing FIELD/refinement/frequency semantics remain.
F/P tables remain N/C-only. Both mode solvers use the same analytic sampler,
retaining `munk.f90`'s f32 `eps` initialization and f32 `5000.0/N` step promotion.
No existing golden or tolerance is changed.

The five new fixtures are **derived**, not unmodified original pairs:

- `MunkLeakyPartialP/S`: relative to `MunkLeakyPartialLoss`, change the titles
  and N→P/S only, including `.flp` titles; keep seven knots, NG=800, RMax=0,
  0.8 W bottom loss, 30 modes (9 leaky) and 36 point-source pressures.
- `PekerisComplexSpline3`: derives from the real `PekerisSpline3` by changing
  title, `SVN`→`SVW`, NG 100→101, bottom W loss 0→0.25 and
  cHigh 1700→2000 m/s. Three nonuniform knots and RMax=1000 km remain.
  Coherent line-source `.flp` is copied from Pekeris. It has four modes
  (one leaky), nine pressures and reference meshes 1/2/4.
- `MunkAnalyticComplex`: derives from original `MunkAnalytic.env` by changing
  title, NG 0→2003, RMax 200→1000 km and modal receiver samples 501→11
  (0..5000 m endpoints). Source is still 1000 m; the separately derived
  coherent line-source `MunkAnalytic.flp` is reused unchanged (25 pressures).
  All 102 modes are compared; reference meshes are 1/2/4.
- `MunkLeakyPchipBroadband`: derives from the partial PCHIP case by changing
  title, NG 800→803, RMax 0→1000 km, adding sixth-slot B and frequencies
  75/50/62.5/50 Hz. FIELD changes only its title. Meshes 1/2/4 use intervals
  1204/2409/4818, 803/1606/3212 and 1003/2007/4015; repeated 50 Hz retains
  its own block. It has 45/30/37/30 modes and 36 pressures per block.

Three pinned runs per final fixture yield identical `.mod/.shd`. Binaries are
copied unchanged; `.prt` only trims trailing whitespace (timings are not an
identity requirement). Direct and actual CLI-HDF5 comparisons check all modes,
shapes, speeds, attenuation and pressures. Local pressure errors for P/S are
8.33e-9 each, three-point spline 2.99e-8, analytic 6.10e-9 and broadband
at most 7.46e-9. Numeric validation still rejects spline undershoot and
P/S coefficient overflow.

Two **unmodified original environments** are also run three times with
KRAKENC, with 102 modes/25 pressures each: `tests/Munk/MunkS.env` (S) and
`MunkAnalytic.env` (A), automatic NG and RMax=200 km (reference meshes 1/2).
MunkS was a **SCOOTER** fixture in upstream `runtests.m`; this is an environment
reuse, not SCOOTER support. Their identical original three-line `.flp` fails
in pinned FIELD (`Bad integer for item 1 in list input`); both receive the
separately derived coherent `MunkAnalytic.flp`, never a claim of original-pair
acceptance. Three reference `.mod/.shd` pairs are identical, and full direct /
actual CLI-HDF5 differential passes (local pressures 1.87e-9 / 3.73e-9).
Original binaries stay out of Git. Local manifests, source/compiler record
and original-pair rejection log are under `target/reference/profile-stage`.

The unmodified original **BroadBand/MunkK** remains accepted at 50/500 Hz
through **KRAKEN**. A local KRAKENC S-profile run matches 50 Hz (102 modes,
501,501 pressures), but 500 Hz exceeds its unchanged 300M root-work budget.
Reference generation for both frequencies is only smoke, not Rust acceptance.
An ignored fresh-CI CLI regression asserts exit 3 at frequency index 1,
retains an old output and removes scratch after 50 Hz succeeds. No partial
file, truncated reference modes or budget/tolerance increase is used.

## TabRefCoef input and resource provenance

`TabRefBrcN/C` and `TabRefIrcN/C` are **derived inputs**, not the original
TabRefCoef workflow. The water SSP endpoints and modal depths come from
`neggradC_brc/irc`; title, frequency 500→50 Hz, NG 1000→100 and N/C interpolation
are explicit changes. Their reduced `.flp` has ranges 0/0.5/1 km, receivers
0/50/100 m and zero offsets. N variants use a line source at 0 m (also endpoint
extension); C variants use a point source at 10 m. All retain vacuum top,
RMax=0 and blank restarts. Their tables are **constructed**, not generated by
BOUNCE or thinned copies of its outputs:

- BRC: 0/45/90 degrees, magnitude 0.8 and unwrapped phase 170/190/210 degrees.
- IRC: real k² 0.01/0.03/0.05, powers 0/10/20; stored f is
  `(0.01+0.01i) * 10^-power`, stored g is `1 * 10^-power`.

Three pinned runs of each final fixture yield identical `.mod/.shd`. Raw
binaries are copied unchanged; `.prt` only removes trailing whitespace. The
same committed/fresh comparator checks every mode, phase-aligned shape,
printed/binary wave number, attenuation, phase/group speed and pressure. Local
maximum pressure errors for BRC N/C are 0 / 7.46e-9, and IRC N/C are
0 / 1.67e-8, at the existing 2e-6 pressure and 1e-6 shape tolerances.
Unit regressions separately lock IRC polynomial/scaling/domain semantics, BRC
unwrapped phase/f32 brackets, and the pinned GNU real-component grouping.

For the **unmodified original** `neggradC_geo/brc/irc` `.env/.flp`, upstream
`runtests.m` selects KRAKENC (real KRAKEN does not support these tables).
The directory contains **no `.brc/.irc`**. `tools/reference/prepare-tabref.sh`
copies the original bytes and uses rebuilt pinned BOUNCE to generate resources
from original `neggradB.env`. Docker explicitly deletes archived `bounce.exe`
and `bounce.o` before compiling with the recorded flags. Three independent
runs generate identical tables and `.mod/.shd`; manifests and build information
remain under `target/reference/TabRefCoef`. Reference smoke alone is not Rust
acceptance: fresh CI compares the full Rust result and actual CLI HDF5 readback.
Original binaries/tables are not committed. The original `.env` samples
1..100 m; original `.flp` requests 0..100 m. Neither input is changed to avoid
FIELD endpoint extension. Each result is compared to its own reference; BRC,
IRC and geo need not agree. Local pressure errors are respectively 2.75e-7,
5.96e-8 and 5.96e-8. Tolerances and numerical budgets are unchanged.
Neither repeatability nor these comparisons prove every mathematical root was
found; table seeding retains the fixed reference's branch-sensitive search.

## Water-material checkpoint reference artifacts

These are **derived** fixture pairs, not unmodified upstream VolAtt inputs.
`WaterLossN/C/P/S`, `WaterLossUnitN/M/F/Q/L`, `WaterLossPower` and
`WaterLossThorp/Fg/Bio` derive from committed `PekerisSpline3.env`:
preserve 100 m, nonuniform nodes at 0/43/100 m (1500/1530/1500 m/s), density 1,
fluid bottom 1700 m/s / density 1.5, cLow/cHigh 1400/1700 and RMax=1000 km.
Change the title, interpolation/loss options, NG=101, and node/bottom absorption.
Their FIELD input is the existing `Pekeris.flp`, copied byte-for-byte.

Base W losses at the three nodes are 0.03/0.025/0.02 dB/wavelength, with
0.25 dB/wavelength bottom loss. N/M/F/Q/L variants encode equivalent loss
at nominal 50 Hz, with full-precision conversion values written into each input.
Power-law m uses the equivalent 50 Hz dB/m values, distinct water beta/fT
1.5/60 Hz and bottom 0.75/70 Hz, and ordered 75/50/62.5/50 Hz (including a repeat).
Volume variants use 500 Hz, NG=1003 and zero explicit absorption: Thorp;
FG with T=10, salinity=35, pH=8, mean depth=50 m; or two overlapping bio layers
(0,80,500,2.5,0.25) and (43,120,600,3,0.15). Biological loss is converted at
SSP knots and excluded from the half-space (`UpdateHSLoss` uses HUGE depth).

`WaterLossLeaky` derives from `MunkLeakyPchipBroadband.env/.flp`: retain
the seven-node 1 km PCHIP profile, NG=803, 0.8 W bottom loss, cHigh=1700,
RMax=1000 km and 75/50/62.5/50 Hz with point-source geometry; add node water
absorption `0.015 + depth_m * 0.00001` dB/wavelength. Only the title and node
absorption records change; inherited values are written explicitly.

All 27 workflows used the pinned version/compiler/flags above. Three runs
per workflow produced byte-identical `.mod/.shd`; `.prt` below is the first
run with only trailing whitespace removed (timings are not required identical).
Both Rust API and actual CLI-HDF5 comparisons pass at unchanged tolerances:
36 frequency blocks, 404 modes, 432 pressures; local max |dp|=3.332001e-8.
First-mesh shapes/group speeds, refined k, signed imaginary k, every frequency
and pressure are checked. Existing golden files and tolerances are unchanged.
Fresh Linux CI is configured; this local checkpoint is not final CI evidence.

## Smooth-boundary and top-TRC reference artifacts

These fourteen input pairs are **derived**, not original upstream boundary/TRC
workflows. The nine `FluidBoundary{V,R,A}{V,R,A}` pairs derive from `WaterLossS`:
retain 50 Hz, 100 m spline water at 0/43/100 m (1500/1530/1500 m/s), node losses
0.03/0.025/0.02 W, NG=101 and RMax=1000 km. Change only title/boundaries, add
1900 m/s / density 1.1 / 0.3 W top material for A, remove bottom material for
V/R, and extend modal samples to 0/25/75/99/100 m. FIELD is byte-identical
`Pekeris.flp`. A bottom retains 1700 m/s / density 1.5 / 0.25 W. Both backends
compare the whole trapped spectrum. `FluidBoundaryAir` derives from AA: C water,
343 m/s / density 0.0012 / zero explicit top loss, RMax=0 and KRAKENC only.

`FluidRigidPlaneLoss` derives from `PekerisRigidPlane.env/.flp`: retain its
18.492816128363287 Hz, 77.45263063369381 m, 1595.8580929574603 m/s constant
water, rigid ends and original geometry; add 0.03 W water loss and use NG=68.
The automatic NG=17 variant changes the searched KRAKENC mode count across
meshes and is explicitly rejected, not truncated to the first-mesh spectrum.

`FluidTrcN/C` derive from `PekerisComplexGradient.env`: retain 1500→1520 m/s,
100 m, density 1 and cHigh=2000; set top F, NG=101, cLow=1550, 0.25 W A-bottom
loss and modal samples 0/25/75/99/100 m. `FluidTrcRigid` replaces that C case's
bottom with R and removes its half-space record. FIELD is `Pekeris.flp`;
constructed `.trc` bytes are copied from `TabRefBrcN.brc` (0/45/90 degrees,
0.8 magnitude, unwrapped 170/190/210-degree phases). The accepted spectral
window is propagating at pinned BCImpedancec's last-node inside-water speed.
An earlier cLow=1400 experiment had a growing reference root and is **not**
accepted; evanescent TRC, top P and simultaneous top/bottom tables are rejected.

All 24 workflows use the pinned version/compiler/flags at the top of this file.
Three runs produce byte-identical `.mod/.shd`; `.prt` is run1 with trailing
whitespace removed, not timing-normalized. Every mode and pressure passes the
existing API and actual CLI-HDF5 comparator: **68 modes, 202 pressures**, local
max |dp|=9.424322e-8. Combined with water-material fixtures: 51 workflows,
60 frequency blocks, 472 modes and 634 pressures. No old golden or tolerance
changes; configured fresh Linux CI is separate from these local results.

## Layered fluids: derived acceptance and original failure input

The same pinned source/compiler/flags above generated all artifacts. Twenty-one
**derived** pairs give 41 workflows (both engines except leaky broadband), 50
frequency blocks, 530 modes and 4,902 pressures. Each workflow's `.mod/.shd` was
byte-identical in three independent runs. Only trailing whitespace was removed
from `.prt`; timings were not normalized. Old goldens/tolerances were not changed.
All frequencies, medium records, modes and pressures pass direct API and actual
CLI-HDF5 comparisons; the local maximum pressure error is 2.64e-9.

### Derivation

- `LayeredFluidN/C/P/S`: constructed 50 Hz, interfaces 0/70/140 m, NG=101/83,
  densities 1/1.6. First-layer knots (depth, speed, W loss) are
  (0,1500,.02), (31,1520,.015), (70,1510,.01); second-layer knots are
  (70,1450,.035), (89,1480,.03), (140,1460,.025). Vacuum top, A bottom
  cp=1800/rho=2/W=.25, cLow/cHigh=1400/1800, RMax=1000 km. Modal/FIELD
  depths include 70 and both sides; point-source FIELD has sources 31/70/105 m,
  seven depths and ranges .5/1/2 km (63 pressures). P/S are independent per layer.
- `LayeredBoundaryVV/VR/RV/RR/RA/AV/AR/AA` change only the N fixture's title
  and outer boundaries; the original N fixture already covers VA. A top adds
  cp=1900/rho=1.1/W=.3; V/R remove the corresponding half-space record.
- `LayeredFluidThree` splits the second layer at 105 m (NG=83) and adds
  105..140 m, NG=127, rho=2.2, cp=1600..1570, W=.04...035. It explicitly
  uses cHigh=1700 and refinement (four modes). `LayeredFluidThreeWide` keeps
  cHigh=1800 and sets RMax=0 (all five modes), with its own complete reference.
  The cHigh=1800/RMax=1000 km experiment is **not accepted**: pinned KRAKENC
  finds 5 then 4 roots while Rust retains 5; this is a known refinement-parity
  gap, not currently a Rust input rejection. Neither accepted reference is
  trimmed to mimic this experiment; none proves all mathematical secant roots.
- `LayeredFluidPlane` uses C interpolation, cp=1500 and W=.02 throughout,
  with two rigid outer boundaries and the same density jump (six modes).
- `LayeredFluidPower`: m units; nominal 50 Hz W node losses above are encoded
  as dB/m (`W * 50 / cp`). Headers use beta/fT=1.5/60 and .75/70; bottom
  options use 1.25/55. B frequencies 75/50/62.5/50 Hz are retained, including
  repeats; both solvers refine on meshes 1/2/4. NG is scaled before truncation
  independently for each layer (75 Hz: 151/124, 303/249, 606/498).
- `LayeredFluidLeaky`: P fixture with cHigh=2300 and the same ordered repeated
  frequencies; KRAKENC only, meshes 1/2/4, including every leaky reference mode.
- `LayeredFluidBio`: 500 Hz, NG=1003/809, N material unit and zero explicit
  node/half-space loss. Biological layers (0,70,500,2.5,.25) and
  (70,140,600,3,.15) overlap inclusively at the interface; no biological loss
  is added in the A half-space (reference HUGE depth).
- `LayeredFluidFractional` changes the N interface/total depths to
  70.1259131234/140.1293712391 m, including the matching geometry/SSP records;
  nearest interface-side depths remain separate. It checks reference f32 mesh
  accumulation and sampling without averaging or flattening layers.
- `LayeredDoubleRefined` derives from unmodified `tests/TLslices/double.env`,
  changing title and doubling NG=100/200/200 to 200/400/400. Its FLP is the
  **unmodified official common** `tests/TLslices/fieldbat.flp`, copied as
  directed by upstream `runtests.m`; 42 modes and 501 line-source pressures
  pass per engine. This does not establish original `double` acceptance.
- `LayeredNormalization` derives from `tests/TLslices/normal.env`, changing
  only title and bottom cs=2000 to 0 (cp=4000/rho=3). It uses the same original
  common FLP: 44 modes/501 pressures per engine. Original normal/flused/elsed
  contain elastic material and are not accepted here.

`OriginalLayeredDouble.env` is byte-identical to the upstream `double.env` and
its `.flp` is byte-identical to official `fieldbat.flp`. It is a **failure fixture**,
not an accepted golden. Pinned KRAKEN changes 43 to 42 modes on multipliers 1/2;
both Rust backends return a mode-count-change diagnostic. CLI tests verify no
partial result, preservation of old output and scratch cleanup, also after three
successful frequency blocks when the fourth hits the unchanged root-work limit.
Analytic Munk and F/P/TRC stay single-layer; density gradients, shear/elasticity
and multi-profile FIELD remain excluded. Budgets are totals across all layers.

Upstream source SHA-256 (paths inside the fixed archive):

```text

17365befbd165b21fa3b89d80d7805dd5a51f240af491c8dd30bf27a7a399f2d  tests/TLslices/fieldbat.flp
ff6c4c3516e0f7471793f9ac2e7708d61d84db0db84fd1ab513383b40214fa07  tests/TLslices/runtests.m

## Elastic half-spaces: original and derived acceptance

Same unmodified source/compiler/flags. Eighteen input pairs (15 derived, three
original) give 27 workflows, 33 frequency blocks, 415 modes and 4,707 pressures.
Every .mod/.shd is byte-identical in three independent runs. Only trailing
whitespace is stripped from .prt; timings remain. Direct API and actual CLI/HDF5
compare every mode/pressure and elastic P/S material at unchanged numerical
tolerances; the local maximum pressure error is 6.67e-8. HDF5 is not a golden.

| Inputs | Engines | Modes per frequency | Pressures per engine |
|---|---|---|---:|
| ElasticHalfBottomN/C/P/S | both, each input | 5 | 63 |
| ElasticHalfTopN/C/P/S | KRAKENC, each input | 6 | 63 |
| ElasticHalfBothN/C/P/S | KRAKENC, each input | 5 | 63 |
| ElasticHalfLeaky | KRAKENC | 5 | 63 |
| ElasticHalfPower (75/50/62.5/50 Hz) | both | 7/5/6/5 | 252 |
| ElasticHalfShearOnly (line source) | both | 5 | 63 |
| OriginalElasticScholte | both | 45 | 501 |
| OriginalElasticNormal | both | 44 | 501 |
| OriginalElasticFlused | both | 46 | 501 |

**Derived:** ElasticHalfBottomN/C/P/S reuse the corresponding LayeredFluidN/C/P/S
inputs/FLP, changing title and A bottom to cp=4000, cs=2000, rho=2, W P/S loss=.25/.4.
ElasticHalfTopN/C/P/S retain the original acoustic bottom and add an A top with
cp=4500, cs=2300, rho=1.1, W P/S loss=.3/.5; Both applies both elastic changes.
All finite media remain fluid; cLow/cHigh=1400/1800 and RMax=1000 km are unchanged.
ElasticHalfLeaky uses N, cp=3000/cs=1000 at the bottom with the same losses and
all other parameters unchanged (radiating shear; KRAKENC only).
ElasticHalfPower derives from BottomP: W is encoded as m at nominal 50 Hz using
W*50/cp at fluid/P nodes and W*50/cs for shear loss; layer beta/fT=1.5/60 and
.75/70, bottom=1.25/55, B in the sixth slot, frequencies 75/50/62.5/50 Hz.
ElasticHalfShearOnly derives from BottomN: all P/water losses are zero, shear
W=.4 remains and FLP RAOC becomes XAOC. Real KRAKEN intentionally has zero elastic
attenuation as in the oracle; KRAKENC retains shear attenuation.

**Original:** OriginalElasticScholte/Normal/Flused are byte copies of pinned
`tests/TLslices/scholte.env`, `normal.env`, `flused.env` respectively. No title,
NG or shear edit is made. Each FLP is the exact common `fieldbat.flp` selected by
upstream `runtests.m`, not a newly constructed geometry. Original normal keeps
bottom cs=2000, unlike the independently accepted earlier LayeredNormalization.
Fresh CI compares their bytes to the installed pinned sources before running.

```

All 117 records (36 inputs + 81 artifacts) are in
[`elastic-halfspace.sha256`](elastic-halfspace.sha256), paths relative to the
fixture directory; verify with `shasum -a 256 -c golden/elastic-halfspace.sha256`.
No earlier golden or tolerance was changed. KRAKEN elastic top is explicitly
rejected; finite solids are outside this half-space checkpoint and failed
constructed slow-interface probes are **not** accepted. Original elsed/ice now
pass the separate finite-cap checkpoint below. The existing layered exception
does not waive any elastic failure. See the [half-space checkpoint](../../../../../docs/kraken-elastic-halfspaces.md).

## Homogeneous finite elastic layers

25 pairs (23 derived/constructed, two originals), 50 workflows / 56 blocks /
933 modes / 10,536 pressures. Every mode, shape and pressure passes API and actual
CLI/HDF5 comparison at unchanged tolerances; local max |dp|=5.960464477539063e-8.
MOD/SHD are byte-identical across three independent unmodified pinned runs.
PRT timings remain intact; only trailing whitespace is removed. Rust HDF5 is
never a reference artifact. Verify all 200 input/artifact records from fixtures:
`shasum -a 256 -c golden/finite-elastic.sha256`.

**Original:** OriginalElasticSediment.env = TLslices elsed.env (46 modes per
engine); OriginalElasticIce.env = ice.env (44 per engine). No title, NG, shear,
loss or source edit. Both FLPs are exact fieldbat.flp (501 pressures per engine),
selected by the official runtests.m. Installed pinned-source byte checks:

```text
71df9c66a6bc394f727f41cc9bd3afdd397ffb49318d86fdad4e2c7594cbc0d5  tests/TLslices/elsed.env
cf71bb25552e641b94d8514ea5d0c85722ec458a900c4478d2651142b38119e5  tests/TLslices/ice.env
17365befbd165b21fa3b89d80d7805dd5a51f240af491c8dd30bf27a7a399f2d  tests/TLslices/fieldbat.flp
```

**Derived:** FiniteSingleIce/Sediment C/P/S change only title/interpolation of
the originals. KRAKEN and KRAKENC pass all six. **Constructed:**
FiniteElasticBottom/Top/Both N/C/P/S originate from LayeredFluidN/C/P/S,
retaining layered-fluid SSP/loss/geometry, with finite homogeneous sediment
140..170 m cp2200/cs900/rho1.8 (.15/.3 W), cap 0..20 m cp3000/cs1400/rho1
(.3/1 W), or both. Where present, the outer elastic A is cp4000/cs2000/rho2
(.25/.4 W); bottom-only outer top remains vacuum. The modal interval starts
in the fluid, not at physical depth zero. ShearOnly sets water/P losses to zero
and retains only solid shear loss. Power preserves 75/50/62.5/50 Hz and
per-medium m power laws/fractional NG scaling. Vacuum/Rigid replace only the
outer bottom A and its record. Stack splits both caps into two independently
meshed/materially distinct solids, not a fluid average. These 17 constructed
pairs pass both engines. Real TopN/ShearOnly have 4/3 modes; ordered Power has
8/6/6/6. Real Solve2 carries its search bound across meshes/frequencies rather
than cropping to a reference count. When later meshes reduce M, pinned WriteMode
can leave first-mesh records beyond the declared spectrum; the comparator checks
all declared modes/shapes/pressures and bounds those stale trailing records.
No other record-length/count check or numerical tolerance is relaxed.
See [finite-cap scope and stiffness semantics](../../../../../docs/kraken-finite-elastic-layers.md).

Existing half-space, layered and single-fluid goldens/tolerances are unchanged.

## Single-profile FIELD extensions

Three small derived pairs close the initial range-independent FIELD options
without claiming every combination. `FieldScaled` copies Pekeris except titles
and changes FLP `X` to `S`; it runs through KRAKEN. `FieldPattern` and
`FieldIncoherent` copy `PekerisComplexBlank` except titles. The former changes
FLP `O` to `*` and consumes a constructed seven-point dB `.sbp`; the latter
changes coherent `C` to incoherent `I`. Both run through KRAKENC so complex
modal contributions are retained.

All three MOD/SHD pairs are byte-identical across three pinned runs. Complete
API and actual CLI/HDF5 comparison checks 11 modes and 27 pressures at the
existing tolerances; maximum local |dp| is 3.332000937312528e-8. The CLI hashes
the exact SBP snapshot and records geometry/addition/pattern metadata. Verify
the seven inputs and nine reference artifacts with
`shasum -a 256 -c golden/single-profile-field.sha256`. PRT trailing whitespace
alone is removed; Rust HDF5 is not a golden. Multi-profile adiabatic/coupled
FIELD is not part of these fixtures.

## Multi-profile FIELD

`ProfilesAd` / `ProfilesCm` are constructed four-profile Pekeris derivatives,
with depths 100/120/80/100 m and full-interval samples. Both use initial FIELD
cap 2 and eight receiver ranges; CM can excite higher modes after an interface.
All 13 modes and 24 pressures per path are checked, including depth changes,
bottom half-space tails, exact interfaces, skipped segments and the final
constant-profile continuation. These are not byte-original upstream inputs.

The committed `original/Gulf/gulf_rd.env`, `gulf_ad.flp`, `gulf_cm.flp` preserve
pinned upstream bytes, including CRLF line endings. Fresh CI pairs unchanged files under `GulfAd` / `GulfCm`
working stems and verifies them against the pinned image source tree. Each path
checks all 497 modes over eight profiles and all 501,501 pressures. No large
Gulf binaries or Rust HDF5 are promoted to committed goldens.

All four MOD/SHD pairs are byte-identical in three pinned runs. API and actual
CLI/HDF5 differential pass the existing tolerances, with maximum local |dp|
`4.1159031748919954e-10`. PRT trailing whitespace alone is removed. The 13-record
`multi-profile.sha256` manifest locks seven input files and six small artifacts.
The unchanged reference source hashes are:

| v2023.5 source | SHA-256 |
|---|---|
| `KrakenField/EvaluateADMod.f90` | `d6ff17945ca0c83717f6b0bb9e4b66cf5aed83b9e54348e2323b613687b62785` |
| `KrakenField/EvaluateCMMod.f90` | `2072109901a230bb1e233372ca95d2babee39753f58ae3b3a68419bdd6ec6d0c` |
